We expect a continued gradual reduction of the CRE loan concentration ratio during the fourth quarter 2026, followed by a modest increase at March 31, 2027 due to the capital impact of the cash consideration to be paid at the closing of the Providence and Bluevine acquisitions anticipated in early 2027.

Currently, we expect that Valley's CET1 capital ratio will remain near the midpoint of the 10.50 to 11.00 percent range through December 31, 2026 as previously projected and disclosed in Valley's Annual Report.
Between June 30, 2024, when the federal funds target rate reached its peak, and September 30, 2026, our cumulative deposit beta was 49 percent.
The increase in time deposits was largely driven by higher indirect customer CD balances and deposits generated from our targeted retail CD offerings.
We currently expect total deposit growth for the full-year 2026 to be at or above the high end of the 5 to 7 percent range previously disclosed in Valley's Annual Report.
As a result, we cannot guarantee that we will be able to increase or maintain deposit levels at or near those reported at September 30, 2026.
We currently anticipate net interest income growth for the full year of 2026 to be at the high end of the 11 to 13 percent range previously disclosed in Valley's Annual Report.
While we are optimistic about the projected net interest income through the fourth quarter 2026, our forecasts include several uncertain assumptions, including projected funding costs.

Overall, we expect the level of professional and legal fees reported for the third quarter 2026 to continue into the fourth quarter of 2026 due to ongoing business transformation activities, as well as additional expense related to the pending acquisitions of Providence and Bluevine.

The decrease in our effective tax rate for the third quarter 2026 as compared to both prior periods was primarily due to the purchase of additional tax credits in excess of amounts previously anticipated during the third quarter 2026.
Based on the current information available, we anticipate that our effective tax rate will be approximately 20 percent for the full year 2026.

In assessing whether a credit loss exists, we compare the present value of cash flows expected to be collected from the security with the amortized cost basis of the security.

We do not intend to sell any of the AFS debt securities in an unrealized loss position prior to recovery of our amortized cost basis, and we believe it is more likely than not that we will not be required to sell any of our securities prior to recovery of our amortized cost bas is.
To measure the expected credit losses on HTM debt securities that have loss expectations, we utilize a third party discounted cash flow model.

Based on our current projections, we expect total loan growth for the full year of 2026 to be above the high end of the 4 to 6 percent range previously disclosed in Valley's Annual Report.

Under CECL, our methodology to establish the allowance for loan losses has two basic components: (i) a collective reserve component for estimated expected credit losses for pools of loans that share common risk characteristics and (ii) an individually evaluated reserve component for loans that do not share risk characteristics, consisting of collateral dependent loans.

The Federal Reserve's recent rate hike to a target federal funds rate range of 3.75 - 4.00 percent at September 30, 2026 was not part of the Moody's Baseline forecast in September 2026, however, the impact of the increase is not expected to be material to our weighted economic forecast.
